exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated access allows adversaries to enumerate and access code repositories without credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of authentication enables direct data collection from code repositories.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Dependency confusion attacks exploit proxy routing to substitute malicious packages for legitimate dependencies.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: Routing proxy misconfigurations can introduce poisoned dependencies into the build pipeline.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Invalid Code Signature
exploitedBy.relevance: Without enforced artifact signing, adversaries can distribute artifacts with invalid or missing signatures.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Gatekeeper Bypass
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of signing enforcement allows bypassing trust controls that verify artifact authenticity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Overprivileged service accounts provide attackers with excessive cloud access upon credential compromise.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
exploitedBy.relevance: Overprivileged service accounts may be abused to obtain or maintain elevated cloud access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Compromised overprivileged service account tokens can be used directly for unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted transport exposes artifacts to interception and exfiltration over unprotected channels.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabled encryption at rest makes cloud-stored artifacts directly readable if storage is accessed.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Secrets Management Stores
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted storage may expose secrets and credentials stored alongside artifacts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Compromise Host Software Binary
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted overwrite allows adversaries to replace legitimate artifacts with malicious binaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: An overly broad proxy allow list can permit traffic routing through unauthorized external proxies.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-hop Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient scoping allows adversaries to chain proxies to obscure malicious traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Secrets embedded in artifact metadata represent unsecured credentials exposed to anyone accessing the artifact.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Incomplete audit logging limits detection of adversarial log enumeration and tampering activities.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Configuration Repository
exploitedBy.relevance: Without complete audit logs, unauthorized access to configuration repositories goes undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched repository software contains known vulnerabilities that can be exploited by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Groups
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can enumerate cloud permission groups to identify and exploit inadequate repository segmentation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Permission Groups Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient permission segmentation enables discovery and abuse of overly permissive repository access groups.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: CDNs
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabled checksum validation on proxy caches enables serving of tampered artifacts from cached/CDN content.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing lifecycle/cleanup policies directly relate to uncontrolled artifact retention and deletion management.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Hide Artifacts
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive retention without cleanup can allow stale or malicious artifacts to persist and remain hidden.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Unmonitored certificate expiry creates opportunities for adversaries to exploit expired or substituted certificates.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Expired TLS certificates can be identified and exploited by adversaries through reconnaissance of digital certificates.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Inhibit System Recovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Without backup and recovery configuration, adversaries can more effectively inhibit system recovery after an attack.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data Destruction
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of backup policies amplifies the impact of data destruction attacks against the repository.
